title: Atomic-Scale Structure and Chemistry of Yttrium-Doped Σ3 and Σ67 Grain Boundaries in Magnesium Aluminate Spinel
content: Grain boundaries (GBs) significantly influence the mechanical [1] and electronic properties of materials [2] through their grain growth kinetics and final microstructures [3]. These interfaces can be engineered by incorporating dopant atoms that segregate to GBs, representing a great opportunity for tailoring many properties. To effectively modify GBs as a strategy to control properties, a detailed understanding of the atomic-scale configurations and chemistry of doped GBs is crucial. Dopant atoms, such as yttrium (Y), tend to segregate to GBs in magnesium aluminate spinel (MgAl2O4), potentially modifying the local GB environment [4]. However, the precise atomic arrangements and elemental composition of doped GBs in spinel remain largely unknown. For this reason, well-defined spinel bicrystals with specific GB orientations (Σ3 and Σ67) were fabricated, doped with Y, and characterized using advanced electron microscopy techniques. Quantitative electron energy-loss spectrometry (EELS) and X-ray energy dispersive spectrometry (XEDS) analyses were used to probe chemistry in the GBs vicinity and atomic-resolution high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) imaging was utilized to elucidate the GB structure and preferential Y-atom positions.
